newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Work begins on longest Latin America gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Work begins on longest Latin America gas pipeline.

text.p: Construction of Latin America's longest gas pipeline started on Friday along the border between Bolivia and Brazil, after half a century of tortuous negotiations.

The pipeline, expected to be completed by December 1998, will initially transport eight million cubic meters of natural gas a day from Santa Cruz in Bolivia to Brazil's industrial states of Sao Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul.
After the fifth year the flow is expected to increase to up to 30 million cubic meters a day.

"This work is an example for the Americas and a hope for us," Bolivian President Gonzalo Sanched de Lozado told his Brazilian counterpart, Fernando Henrique Cardoso, at a ceremony marking the launch of construction work.
"It can only be compared to the Itaipu hydroelectric dam," Cardoso said, describing it as "the result of cooperation, understanding and capacity for joint work."
The Itaipu project, the world's largest hydroelectric generator, is on the border between Brazil and Paraguay and is half-owned by each country.
The ceremony was held at an elegant hotel in the border town of Puerto Quijarro, some 1,000 km southeast of La Paz.
Contracts worth $2.0 billion to build the pipeline were signed by the Brazilian state oil company Petrobras with four international consortia.
A second tender to extend the pipeline to Rio Grande do Sul will be awarded in November.

Cardoso said the pipeline, which will span 1,900 miles (3,100 km) and have a diameter of up to 32 inches, may be used in the future to transport gas to a new thermoelectric plant on the border between the two countries.
Sanchez de Lozada said when Bolivia starts exporting natural gas under a 20-year contract, the rate of growth of the Bolivian economy will rise by 1.5 percentage points from the current four percent.
The project has been financed by the World Bank, the Inter-American Development Bank and the Andean Development Corporation, among other lenders.
